title: Inspect the model limit
summary: A model setting chosen before fitting is a hyperparameter. max_depth limits how many splits a tree can make along a path.
introduction: A model setting chosen before fitting is a hyperparameter. max_depth limits how many splits a tree can make along a path. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A model setting chosen before fitting is a hyperparameter. max_depth limits how many splits a tree can make along a path.

blocks.code:
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
model = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=1, random_state=0)
model.fit([[1], [2], [8], [9]], [0, 0, 1, 1])
print(model.get_depth())
blocks.title: Inspect the model limit

blocks.text: The result is 1. The tree learned one split level for this dataset. A larger limit allows more complex rules.

blocks.text: More complex models can memorise training details instead of learning useful patterns.
